---
title: Convert an address to other types
description: Convert an address to other types
---

The `Address` is an opaque type that represents either a 'default' externally owned account on the Stellar network, or a contract (that may also provide logic for custom externally owned accounts, see [authorization docs](../../../learn/fundamentals/contract-development/authorization#account-abstraction) for details). For the smart contracts it normally doesn't matter which kind of `Address` is used. However, in some contexts it's useful to convert `Address` to/from different data types, such as string or XDR. The conversions have distinctly different purpose depending on whether they happen in the smart contract itself, or in the client code.

## String conversions

The default string format for `Address` is a so called 'string key' (or 'strkey'), defined fully in [SEP-23](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0023.md). The first character shows the kind of key: an account starts with `G`, a muxed account starts with `M`, and a contract starts with `C`. SEP-23 lists the other kinds.

In client code, do not branch on the first character. A matching prefix does not prove that the string is a valid address. Parse the string with the SDK instead: the JavaScript SDK throws on an invalid address and reports the kind in `Address.type`, for example `account`, `contract`, or `muxedAccount`. In Go, `strkey.DecodeAny` returns an error for an invalid string and returns the kind as a version byte. In Java, `new Address(...)` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid string and reports the kind in `getAddressType()`, for example `ACCOUNT`, `CONTRACT`, or `MUXED_ACCOUNT`.

### String Conversions in Client SDKs

Outside of the smart contracts, it is convenient to represent `Address` as string most of the time. It can be stored in string serialization formats such as JSON and XML. Storing addresses as strings in databases can simplify database schema design and queries. Strings are easier to manipulate and are more compatible with user interfaces and APIs. Thus

<CodeGroup>

```js JavaScript
const StellarSdk = require("@stellar/stellar-sdk");

// Example Stellar address
const stellarAddress =
  "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN";
// Create an Address object from string (throws if the string is not valid)
const address = StellarSdk.Address.fromString(stellarAddress);
// Convert the address back to string
const addressToString = address.toString();

// Check the kind of address with `type`, not with the first character
console.log(address.type); // "account"

const contractAddress =
  "CAS3J7GYLGXMF6TDJBBYYSE3HQ6BBSMLNUQ34T6TZMYMW2EVH34XOWMA";
const contract = StellarSdk.Address.fromString(contractAddress);
console.log(contract.type); // "contract"
```

```python Python
from stellar_sdk import Address

# Example Stellar address
stellar_address = "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN"
# Create an Address object from string
address = Address(stellar_address)
# Convert the address back to string
address_to_string = address.address
```

```go Go
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "log"

  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/strkey"
)

func main() {
  // Example Stellar address
  stellarAddress := "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN"
  // Decode the string (returns an error if the string is not valid)
  versionByte, payload, err := strkey.DecodeAny(stellarAddress)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  // Convert the address back to string
  addressToString, err := strkey.Encode(versionByte, payload)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  fmt.Println(addressToString)

  // Check the kind of address with the version byte, not with the first character
  fmt.Println(versionByte == strkey.VersionByteAccountID) // true

  contractAddress := "CAS3J7GYLGXMF6TDJBBYYSE3HQ6BBSMLNUQ34T6TZMYMW2EVH34XOWMA"
  versionByte, _, err = strkey.DecodeAny(contractAddress)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  fmt.Println(versionByte == strkey.VersionByteContract) // true
}
```

```java Java
import org.stellar.sdk.Address;

public class AddressStrings {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Example Stellar address
    String stellarAddress = "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN";
    // Create an Address object from string (throws if the string is not valid)
    Address address = new Address(stellarAddress);
    // Convert the address back to string
    String addressToString = address.toString();
    System.out.println(addressToString);

    // Check the kind of address with getAddressType, not with the first character
    System.out.println(address.getAddressType()); // ACCOUNT

    String contractAddress = "CAS3J7GYLGXMF6TDJBBYYSE3HQ6BBSMLNUQ34T6TZMYMW2EVH34XOWMA";
    Address contract = new Address(contractAddress);
    System.out.println(contract.getAddressType()); // CONTRACT
  }
}
```

</CodeGroup>

### String Conversions in Smart Contracts

It's generally preferred for contracts to operate directly on the `Address` type. String conversions may be useful for specialized use cases, such as passing the Stellar `Address`es to/from other chains.

```rust
use soroban_sdk::{Address, String, Env};

pub fn address_to_string(address: Address) -> String {
    address.to_string()
}

pub fn address_from_string(strkey: String) -> Address {
    Address::from_string(&strkey)
}
```

`Address` can also be built from a string literal, which may be useful for testing.

```rust
let test_address = Address::from_str(
    &env,
    "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN",
);
```

## XDR conversions

XDR is schema-based binary serialization format used by the Stellar network. It is used for all the Stellar blockchain interactions, such as building the transactions, storing data in the ledger, communicating the transaction results etc. Stellar SDKs provide the typed wrappers for all the Stellar XDR data types. Address is represented as `ScAddress` type, which can then be wrapped into `ScVal` which is a type that represents any contract type supported by Stellar contracts.

### XDR Conversions in Client SDKs

On the client side XDR conversions are useful to build the transactions and process the transaction results.

<CodeGroup>

```js JavaScript
// Example Stellar address
const stellarAddress =
  "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN";
// Create an Address object from string
const address = new StellarSdk.Address(stellarAddress);
// Convert the Address to xdr.ScVal
const scVal = address.toScVal();
// Convert scVal structure to the binary format
const scValBuffer = scVal.toXDR("raw");
// Convert the Address to xdr.ScAddress
const scAddress = address.toScAddress();
```

```python Python
from stellar_sdk import Address

# Example Stellar address
stellar_address = 'GBJCHUKZMTFSLOMNC7P4TS4VJJBTCYL3XKSOLXAUJSD56C4LHND5TWUC'
# Create an Address object
address = Address(stellar_address)
# Convert the Address object to an ScAddress
sc_address_xdr = address.to_xdr_sc_address()
```

```go Go
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "log"

  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/xdr"
)

func main() {
  // Example Stellar address
  stellarAddress := "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN"
  // Create an xdr.AccountId from the string
  accountID, err := xdr.AddressToAccountId(stellarAddress)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  // Convert the AccountId to xdr.ScAddress
  // (for a contract address, decode it with strkey.Decode and set ContractId)
  scAddress := xdr.ScAddress{
    Type:      xdr.ScAddressTypeScAddressTypeAccount,
    AccountId: &accountID,
  }
  // Convert the ScAddress to xdr.ScVal
  scVal := xdr.ScVal{Type: xdr.ScValTypeScvAddress, Address: &scAddress}
  // Convert scVal structure to the binary format
  scValBytes, err := scVal.MarshalBinary()
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  fmt.Println(len(scValBytes)) // 44
}
```

```java Java
import org.stellar.sdk.Address;
import org.stellar.sdk.xdr.SCAddress;
import org.stellar.sdk.xdr.SCVal;

public class AddressXdr {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    // Example Stellar address
    String stellarAddress = "GCM5WPR4DDR24FSAX5LIEM4J7AI3KOWJYANSXEPKYXCSZOTAYXE75AFN";
    // Create an Address object from string
    Address address = new Address(stellarAddress);
    // Convert the Address to xdr.SCVal
    SCVal scVal = address.toSCVal();
    // Convert the SCVal structure to the binary format
    byte[] scValBytes = scVal.toXdrByteArray();
    System.out.println(scValBytes.length); // 44
    // Convert the Address to xdr.SCAddress
    SCAddress scAddress = address.toSCAddress();
    System.out.println(scAddress.getDiscriminant()); // SC_ADDRESS_TYPE_ACCOUNT
  }
}
```

</CodeGroup>

### XDR Conversions in Smart Contracts

Smart contracts don't need to explicitly interact with the XDR types, as all the smart contract data types are automatically converted to XDR by the smart contract runtime. Every contract type, including `Address`, can be serialized to XDR bytes. This conversion is useful, for example, for performing hashing in smart contracts. It is also possible to convert the serialized XDR bytes back to contract types, which can be useful in some narrow use cases, such as custom authentication schemes.

Note, that XDR conversions are an advanced feature and are not necessary for most Stellar smart contracts.

Deserializing XDR bytes back into a contract type can fail in two ways. If the bytes hold valid XDR for a value of a different type, the conversion returns an error that the contract can handle. If the bytes are not valid XDR for any value at all, the conversion panics, and the SDK offers no in-contract recovery for that case. Contracts that receive XDR bytes from untrusted sources, such as a custom authentication scheme, should handle the error case and validate the input before relying on it: prefer typed arguments such as `Address` where possible, or verify the byte format in the client that submits the transaction.

```rust
use soroban_sdk::{
    xdr::{FromXdr, ToXdr},
    Address, Bytes, ConversionError, Env,
};

pub fn address_to_xdr_bytes(env: Env, address: Address) -> Bytes {
    address.to_xdr(&env)
}

pub fn address_from_xdr_bytes(env: Env, bytes: Bytes) -> Result<Address, ConversionError> {
    Address::from_xdr(&env, &bytes)
}
```
